rounds.text: Nidhi Granites Ltd is undergoing a strategic pivot and restructuring that creates an under-appreciated turnaround opportunity. Management has actively redeployed resources into new growth avenues, notably acquiring Auro Fintech Private Limited as a wholly-owned subsidiary to drive future expansion [E71]. The company explicitly states that performance is steadily improving with a very promising outlook tied to the addition of this fintech business, and expects to grow with accelerated momentum in the coming year [E63, E64]. Furthermore, the enterprise maintains a pristine balance sheet with zero debt (0.00x debt-to-equity) and flat borrowings at Rs 0.00 Cr [E28, E29], providing financial flexibility during this transition. This operational evolution is already being reflected in market sentiment through steady share price appreciation, including a 90% compounded growth rate over 3 years and a 41.2% twelve-month return [E14, E37], alongside a supportive broader sector tailwind in Construction Materials scored at +0.68 [E59]. Conceded: [E5], [E6], [E7], [E9], [E10], [E11], [E20], [E21], [E45], [E50].

The bull highlights a strategic pivot into fintech through the acquisition of Auro Fintech Private Limited [E71], yet the evidence reveals severe execution collapse with sales growth crashing by -89% over the trailing twelve months and profit growth plunging by -226% [E10, E11]. The claim of an improving operational outlook and accelerated momentum [E63, E64] contradicts the reality of quarterly operating margins collapsing to -571% with a continuous four-quarter downtrend [E21, E23], alongside an annual operating margin drop of -904 percentage points to -876% [E20]. While the bull points to a pristine debt-free balance sheet [E28], this asset-light or inactive stance has yielded an appalling ROCE of -12.4% and an ROE of -10.6% [E5, E6], with a 10-year median ROE of -1% [E16] proving that capital is chronically unproductive rather than efficiently deployed. Conceded: [E71], [E28], [E59]. The bull's reliance on past share price appreciation [E14, E37] masks a deep valuation disconnect where the stock trades at an exorbitant 21.48x price-to-book multiple [E1] despite fundamental value destruction, resulting in a failing rules-based score of 37 out of 100 with high sell confidence [E50].
